name: SAP Fieldglass
description: SAP Fieldglass manages external workers, suppliers, job postings, work orders, statements of work, time, expenses, approvals, invoicing, and related services procurement. Its integration portfolio includes customer-configured connectors, REST APIs, reports, events, and specialized partner workflows.
agentUseSummary: SAP Fieldglass cannot yet be connected through Relay. Official interfaces can read and change private external-workforce and commercial data, including worker profiles, time-processing objects, approvals, analytics, background-check results, and customer-defined events. Relay has no approved module, worker population, field, buyer or supplier role, workflow, operation, or payment-authority contract.

blocked.label: Connect SAP Fieldglass
blocked.description: A customer environment, active API user, approved authentication, application or license key, integration configuration, and role-specific authority are required.

blocked.label: Read external-workforce data
blocked.description: Workers, candidates, profiles, background checks, suppliers, jobs, work orders, statements of work, time, expenses, rates, analytics, invoices, and audit data remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change workforce or procurement records
blocked.description: Submitting, onboarding, updating, approving, rejecting, hiring, ending, time-processing, invoicing, paying, or otherwise changing worker and services-procurement records is blocked.

blocked.label: Administer or bulk-process Fieldglass
blocked.description: Connectors, events, reports, users, identities, application keys, configuration, imports, exports, master-data replication, and bulk extraction are blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw or private interfaces
blocked.description: Arbitrary REST, connector feeds, WSDL services, SCIM, private endpoints, browser automation, credential capture, and privilege probing are blocked.

providerSetup.blocker: SAP Fieldglass exposes a broad, customer-configured external-workforce and services-procurement surface rather than one stable account API. Official integrations include approvals, background checks, worker profiles, time-processing objects, analytics, audit trails, customer-defined publish-subscribe events, connectors, reports, WSDL services, and partner integrations. REST can upload, download, or push private data, and OAuth access can be bound to a valid Fieldglass user through client credentials, SAML, or certificates. The underlying records affect worker access, assignments, rates, time, contractual milestones, invoices, and payments. A generic wrapper would combine personal, employment-like, commercial, and financial authority without an approved purpose or role boundary.
providerSetup.nextAction: Product, external-workforce, procurement, HR, finance, legal, privacy, employment-compliance, security, audit, and customer owners must select one bounded outcome and freeze the customer environment, module, connector or API, worker population, fields, buyer and supplier roles, workflows, operations, approvals, rates, monetary limits, retention, audit, reconciliation, discrimination controls, and incident duties. A Fieldglass administrator must then create a dedicated least-privilege integration identity and configuration. Only after that may Relay implement pinned typed wrappers with strict fields, bounded records, approvals for every mutation, redaction, idempotency, reconciliation, audit, and post-disable denial.

evidence.supports: SAP documents separate APIs and integrations for approvals, analytics, background checks, worker profiles, time processing, events, connectors, reports, audit, and other external-workforce workflows.
The REST API can upload, download, and push integrated private data in JSON or CSV against a customer configuration.
OAuth authentication is customer-environment and user-specific and can use client secrets or license keys, SAML, or customer-configured X.509 certificates.
Access tokens can grant varying degrees of access to multiple private-data APIs and optional application keys come from the customer Configuration Manager account.
Statements of work govern supplier acceptance, workers, deliverables, time, milestones, invoicing, and payment rules.
